deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is dated 1836 April 16 and labelled 'Phys. 4'. It belongs to the bundle 'PH.Induktion'. It is a raw observation and reduction sheet for a swinging magnetometer needle, almost certainly one of the Gauss–Weber damping (induction) experiments of 1836. The motion of the magnet is damped partly by the air and partly, when the circuit is closed, by currents induced in a surrounding coil or copper damper. The header 'Dauer vorausg. 42"50' means 'duration assumed: 42.50 s'. This is a provisional value for one 'Schwingung' in Gauss's sense: one swing from one side to the other, i.e. half a full period.

COLUMN 1 (passage times t_n). Times are recorded for oscillations n = 1–16, 46–48, 187–191, 249–254 and 257–260. Successive differences are about 42.5 s. Two examples:
- t_2 − t_1 = 42.60
- t_3 − t_2 = 42.35

RIGHT-HAND COLUMN (reduced epochs). Gauss forms T_n = t_n − n·42.50 s. Checks:
- n = 1: 3h40'4.45 − 42.5 s = 3h39'21.95.
- n = 46: 4h11'56.45 − 1955 s = 3h39'21.45.
- n = 187: 5h51'48.65 − 7947.5 s = 3h39'21.15.
- n = 260: 6h43'30.95 − 11050 s = 3h39'20.95.
T_n stays at about 21.9–22.3 s for n ≤ 16. It then drifts slowly to about 20.95 at n ≈ 260. The true swing duration is therefore slightly below the assumed value [mine: about 42.50 − 1.0/259 ≈ 42.496 s on average]. The slow change is consistent with the decreasing amplitude.

MIDDLE COLUMNS. For most n there are three numbers:
- A_n: the arc (amplitude) of the swing in scale divisions, falling from 1581.4 to 433.75.
- c_n: the scale reading of the centre or rest position, about 985–994, later about 1012–1014.
- log10 A_n, to 5 places. For example, log10 1581.4 = 3.19904 and log10 433.75 = 2.63724.

DECREMENTS. Gauss takes differences of the logarithms, in units of 1e-5.

Group n = 7–11 (circuit closed, strong damping):
- 3.17532 − 3.15183 = 2349
- 3.15183 − 3.12814 = 2369
- 3.12814 − 3.10396 = 2418
- [mine: the first difference, 2372, is not written.]
- Underlining at n = 11 and n = 13 marks the switch to open circuit. The decrement drops sharply after n = 11 (1913, then 770: transitional).

Open-circuit (air-damping) part:
- 3.07571 − 3.07454 = 117 (n = 14–15).
- (3.07454 − 3.03523)/31 = 126.80 per swing (n = 15 → 46).
- Group 46–48: differences 114 and 135.
- Group means: mean log at n = 47 is 3.03402; mean at n = 189 is 2.86180. Then (3.03402 − 2.86180)/142 = 121.28.
- Group 188–190: differences 242 and 197.
- From the n = 189 mean to the mean of n = 250–252 (2.76455): (2.86180 − 2.76455)/62 = 156.86.
- Group 250–253: differences 156, 135, 128. A repeated value 156.86 under this group is struck out.

Group n = 257–260 (circuit closed again; the jump from n = 253 to n = 257 is the transition):
- 2.70910 − 2.68476 = 2434
- 2.68476 − 2.66082 = 2394
- 2.66082 − 2.63724 = 2358

FINAL REDUCTION (bottom right).
- Mean closed-circuit decrements: (2349 + 2369 + 2418)/3 = 2378.67 ≈ 2379, and (2434 + 2394 + 2358)/3 = 2395.33 ≈ 2395.
- Subtract the air part valid at each time: 127 (≈ 126.80) for the first group. For the second group the illegible '1[?]' is [mine] 140, the mean of 156, 135, 128 = 139.67.
- This gives 2252 and 2255, with mean 2253.
- Hence the induction-only part of the logarithmic decrement is about 0.02253 per swing in log10 units [mine: about 0.0519 natural-log units]. The air part is about 0.0013–0.0014.

SCRAPS, interpretation uncertain:
- 6.76 / 1.6 = 4.225 ≈ '4.2'.
- '530' may be 2253/4.25 ≈ 530. This reading is speculative.
- The faint '2290' is unexplained.

PROBLEM SERVED. The aim is to separate the logarithmic decrement into air resistance and electromagnetic induction (the damping effect of induced currents). The page also corrects the provisional swing duration. Both are inputs to Gauss's and Weber's quantitative induction and damping studies.
errors: 126.80 is computed from single endpoints (n = 15 → 46): 3931/31 = 126.806, which rounds to 126.81. The other two air decrements (121.28, 156.86) use group means. On the mean-based method the first would be about 126.48. This is a methodological inconsistency, not a real error.
The rest-point reading 995.350 at n = 12 departs sharply from its neighbours (about 987). It is probably a transient at the switching moment or a slip (perhaps 985.350).

No arithmetic errors were found. All 33 logarithms checked agree with log10 to 5 decimals. Every reduced epoch T_n = t_n − 42.5n agrees with the right-hand column once the two transcription fixes below (n = 10, n = 258) are applied.
The first difference of the n = 7–11 group (3.19904 − 3.17532 = 2372) is not written, and is not used in the mean 2379.

results.what: Reduction of passage times with an assumed swing duration (T_n = t_n − n·τ) to detect a drift in the true period
results.modern_name: Method of residual epochs (linear-ephemeris residuals / O−C) for oscillation period determination
results.usually_credited_to: Standard astronomical practice; for magnetometers Gauss (Intensitas 1832) and the Gauss–Weber 'Resultate' (1836–41)

results.what: Amplitude decay measured by differences of log10 of the arcs; decrement averaged over groups
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement of a damped harmonic oscillator
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, Göttingen 1830s (Weber's damping papers 1837–38; Gauss in the Resultate)

results.what: Separation of the total decrement into an air-resistance part (~0.0013–0.0014) and an induction part (~0.02253 per swing, log10) by alternately closing and opening the circuit
results.modern_name: Additivity of damping coefficients; electromagnetic (eddy-current/induction) damping measurement
results.usually_credited_to: W. Weber and C.F. Gauss (magnetometer damper, 1836–38)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observation and reduction sheet from the well-documented Gauss–Weber magnetometer and induction-damping work of 1836. Logarithmic decrements and the separation of air and induction damping are known to be theirs. The value lies only in the archival data.

n = 10: the passage time is 3h46'27.30, not 27.70. The digit is overwritten, and the reduced epoch 22.30 together with the 42.5 s spacing requires .30.
n = 258: 6h42'06.00. The reduced epoch 21.00 gives 06; the overwritten digit is 0.
